messages.text:
"A 3D top down RPG life simulator that takes place in a fantasy medieval city with a mix of classic fantasy and adult themes. The game play is like a mix of star dew valley, Fable 3, The Sims, and Red Dead Redemption 2 in different categories, there is farming and homebase management and a fully customizable home plot similar to stardew Valley, fully interactive NPCs and buy able houses and jobs you can work in town like fable, full survival mechanics and relationships and home building and pets like the Sims, and a lively open world with npc greet and taunt abilities and card games and a living breathing open world full of secrets and a full wanted system like in red dead redemption 2. The player should start with nothing and make their way to the top upgrading their home, businesses, character, items, pets, and abilities along the way and interact deeply with every npc in the city with a full relationship system with love and hate bars and friend or foe bars and the option to have a family and recruit your family to adventure with you and have a pet with their own independent stats that you upgrade as a companion along with an entire city filled with NPCs living their daily lives that you can interact with hundreds of different ways both good and bad. You also have a reputation system and an honor system that affects how your treated, stats that affect how your viewed like clothing, reputation, honor, fitness, if your bloody, past interactions, your job, your house, your behavior over time, and tons more. You can either run a business from your home, buy a shop and change it to anything you want in the main city, be an adventurer taking on quests for gold from the town folks, take on bounties and hunt criminals wanted that have evaded the law, work for another npc performing job duties in the form of mini games in another shop in town, be a criminal and rob stores and homes and villagers at the risk of getting arrested or killed and the towns folk hating you if they find out who you are, sending your family to work for passive income as long as you can keep them happy, sell items you find or loot, take on contracts for killing monsters or villagers with both good and bad impacts on your honor or reputation, and much more. Your house starts off an old decrepit single room on a big plot that you have chosen between several different starter options each with their own perks and challenges and you want to get some money and supplies to build your house any way you like, upgrade your items and tools in your inventory, grow crops or raise livestock for coin, produce goods to either sell in a shop or to a shopkeeper, and explore all the secrets of your land plot. You can go into town too and buy new clothing each with different boosts or debuvgs in different areas that affect how your treated in different areas and by different NPCs for example rich people don't like thugs and thugs don't like rich people so dressing like one won't impress the other, get enough money and you can buy a home to sleep in or rent out or gut out and make a new shop or you can buy an existing shop and put up items you either crafter or hired someone to craft for you and sell them or hire a clerk to do it for you just make sure you can pay your employees and space rent and yearly tax or else you risk losing your employees or your business or even committing a crime and possibly being arrested and imprisoned. You can also just relax in town and hit the bar for a drink or to chat with NPCs or to play some cards or dice or drinking games, the bar is full of people and loose women you can try to pick up and this is where all the gossip is heard. If you break the law tho and an npc reports it to a guard or they see it first hand you will be arrested and taken to jail where you will have to go to court and explain yourself and be punished either by work, prison or by things like branding or whipped or the stocks unless you can convince the judge to let you go.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

This is huge. We need to build a well-scoped implementation. Existing game is canvas 2D with menus. We should substantially enhance, not rewrite from scratch entirely? We can add:

1. Camera: 3/4 perspective with a rotation angle and tilt. Could implement a pseudo-3D projection in canvas: world coordinates, camera yaw, follow player. Buildings extruded with rotation. That's complex but doable. Alternatively use CSS 3D transform? Hmm.

Better: implement a "paper diorama" system: render ground plane in isometric-ish projection with camera yaw rotation. Use a simple 3D projection function for world coords plus height: screen = center + rotate(x-cx,y-cy) * scale, with vertical foreshortening. Buildings as extruded prisms with a fixed yaw that affects side faces. The camera rotates smoothly with Q/E or drag, and zooms close to player. This would satisfy "paper Mario style camera" visually: 3D-ish diorama, level with character. Since we have a 2D canvas engine, we can add yaw and perspective.

This is a major rewrite of drawWorld. The current world is 1100x700 flat with buildings drawn axis-aligned. To rotate, easiest: render the world to an offscreen canvas in flat coordinate, then rotate/scale it? That would rotate text and shadows, and not feel 3D. Not good.

Alternative: Use Three.js with low-poly models generated procedurally, camera behind/above player, orbitable. That gives true 3D, 10k-75k poly characters can be procedural (though low). Combat screen as an overlay. This might be cleaner for 3D and camera rotation. But integrating with all existing UI/game logic is significant. We could keep the game's backend state and menus, and replace the canvas renderer with Three.js. However loading Three.js from CDN might fail offline. We can vendor three.min.js by downloading (network available for font/CDN? Google Fonts loaded, so network works in capture). But reliability matters. Could fetch three.module.js from CDN and save locally. Let's check network and download Three.js. Then build a low-poly 3D town with buildings, characters, trees, well, pond. Camera third-person orbit around player, close, level-ish. Paper Mario style.

This is a big change but achievable with Three.js. Need to build:

- Buildings as low-poly meshes (boxes + roof prisms), with signs via canvas textures. Could make 6 buildings.

Could procedurally build characters from primitives (few hundred tris). - Camera rotates via drag/Q/E and follow, with collision-ish.
- Paper Mario style: orthographic-ish perspective, camera slightly above and behind/level, tilt. Use PerspectiveCamera fov 35, positioned at player + offset rotated by yaw, height ~4, distance 10, look at player + height 1.2. This is over-the-shoulder-ish but Paper Mario is side-ish. "level with the player character" suggests camera height near player chest, low angle. We'll set height 3.2, distance 11, look at y=1.2. Rotatable with drag or Q/E. Good.
- Textures: procedural canvas textures for grass, cobblestone, wood, roof, with low-res noise; "improved textures". Use CanvasTexture with repeat. 
- Mobile: joystick DOM + action button dynamic near interactables, camera drag on canvas, attack button context.

- Turn-based combat: trigger when interacting with hostile mobs. Add mobs in world (e.g., "Bog Hound" x=980,650; "Bandit" x=300,620; "Goblin" x=1030,300?) represented as one enemy. - Player character customization: start screen with sex, body build, skin tone, hair style/color, beard, outfit color, name. Render 3D character accordingly. Add scars after death (state.scars++). Clothing can change later via market; update model color/hat.
- Weapons/abilities: add state.weapon ('Wooden Sword'), abilities. Combat damage scales with level/weapon. Weapons can be bought at market.
- Parkour: climb low walls/fences, vault windows, jump gaps, rooftop traversal, fall damage, smooth transitions. With 3D physics-lite: implement jump (Space) with vertical velocity, player y, gravity; collision with low obstacles (fences) climbable/vaultable; roofs accessible via climb at marked ledge? That's complex. Simplified: add obstacles (fences, crates, low walls, gaps) with proximity prompts (Action button "Climb"/"Vault"/"Jump gap"). Pressing action animates player over the obstacle via a tween (smooth arc), then lands on other side. Roofs: a ladder/stack of crates near a building lets you climb to roof; then walking on roof at height 3.5 with fall damage if you jump off. Implement with ground height map: player y = 0 normally; on roof zones, y = roofHeight. Parkour actions tween x,z,y with easing. Add a stamina cost. Fall damage applied if jumping from roof. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D top-down fantasy-medieval life sim RPG inspired by Stardew Valley, Fable 3, The Sims, and Red Dead Redemption 2.
- Latest request: overhaul the game with a close, low, rotatable Paper Mario-style camera; improved mobile textures; virtual joystick; dynamic action button; Sims 4-style NPC conversation overlay with animated portraits, reaction previews, and real-time action queue; Paper Mario-style turn-based combat with attack minigames and active blocking; detailed character customization; parkour/rooftop traversal with fall damage; and more 3D presentation.

## Requirements
- Setting: fantasy medieval city with classic fantasy and tasteful adult themes.
- Systems requested: farming, home plot management, buyable/upgradeable houses, businesses, jobs/minigames, survival, relationships with love/hate, family, pets with stats, NPC daily lives, reputation/honor/wanted system, clothing effects, bounty hunting, crime/arrest/court, card/dice/drinking games, secrets, exploration.
- Start with nothing and progress by upgrading home, businesses, character, items, pets, and abilities.
- New camera: zoomed close to player, roughly level with character, Paper Mario-style 2D/3D hybrid, rotatable.
- Mobile optimization: improved textures, character poly budget target roughly 10,000–75,000 per character (lower-end), virtual joystick, dynamic action button that appears near interactables.
- NPC interaction: Sims 4-style menu over NPC/player, animated zoomed portrait, bubble menu around head, reaction previews that change per choice, actions queued and played in real time.
- Combat: turn-based Paper Mario-style, minigames for attacks, active block, weapons/abilities, mobs represented by one enemy in world but groups in combat, scaled to player.
- Character customization from the start: physical appearance, body, sex, hair, beard, clothing; later changes allowed; scars gained from dying.
- Parkour: climb small walls/fences, hop through windows, jump gaps/rooftops, fall damage, smooth responsive animated transitions.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Rebuild the existing 2D canvas game as a Three.js 3D diorama, keeping the same town, NPCs, economy, and story content.
- Vendor Three.js locally at `vendor/three.min.js` (downloaded from jsdelivr, r152.2) instead of relying on CDN.
- Use a pseudo-paper-diorama floating island with low-poly building/character models, procedural canvas textures, close follow camera, camera orbit drag, and raycast collision pull-in.
- Use a full-screen 3D canvas with overlay HUD rather than the old permanent sidebar, improving mobile immersion.
- Keep the existing map coordinates (1100×700) for game logic and convert to Three world coordinates with scale factor `S = 28` (`toWorld`/`toMap`).
- Start screen becomes a two-column character-creation panel with live 3D character preview behind it.
- Character portraits for the NPC overlay will be animated SVG portraits (blink/breathe/talk) rather than a second WebGL renderer, for mobile performance.
- NPC action queue executes social actions in real time with bond/stat updates and reaction barks.
- Combat uses the same Three renderer with a dedicated paper stage, side camera, enemy group, timing strike bar, and shrinking-ring block prompt.
- Parkour uses tweened arcs between defined points; roof zones trigger fall damage when left.
- Existing save data schema is replaced by localStorage key `hearthHollow3d`; old `hearthSave` data is not migrated.

## Work State

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D top-down fantasy-medieval life sim RPG inspired by Stardew Valley, Fable 3, The Sims, and Red Dead Redemption 2.
- Latest request: overhaul with a close, low, rotatable Paper Mario-style camera; mobile textures/joystick/dynamic action button; Sims 4-style NPC conversation overlay; Paper Mario-style turn-based combat with attack minigames and active blocking; detailed character customization; parkour/rooftop traversal with fall damage; more 3D presentation.

## Requirements
- Fantasy medieval city with classic fantasy and tasteful adult themes.
- Systems: farming, home plot management, buyable/upgradeable houses, businesses, jobs/minigames, survival, relationships (love/hate), family, pets with stats, NPC daily lives, reputation/honor/wanted system, clothing effects, bounty hunting, crime/arrest/court, card/dice/drinking games, secrets, exploration.
- Start with nothing and progress by upgrading home, businesses, character, items, pets, abilities.
- Camera zoomed close to player, roughly level with character, Paper Mario 2D/3D hybrid, rotatable.
- Mobile: improved textures, character poly target ~10,000–75,000, virtual joystick, dynamic action button near interactables.
- NPC interaction: Sims 4-style menu over NPC/player, animated zoomed portrait, bubble menu around head, reaction previews per choice, actions queued and played in real time.
- Combat: turn-based Paper Mario-style, attack minigames, active block, weapons/abilities, groups shown as one world mob but multiple in combat, scaled to player.
- Character customization from start: physical appearance, body, sex, hair, beard, clothing; later changes allowed; scars gained from dying.
- Parkour: climb small walls/fences, hop through windows, jump gaps/rooftops, fall damage, smooth responsive animations.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Rebuilt the old 2D canvas game as a Three.js 3D diorama, keeping town/NPC/economy/story content.
- Vendored Three.js r152.2 at `vendor/three.min.js`.
- Paper-diorama floating island, low-poly models, procedural canvas textures, close follow camera, orbit drag, raycast camera pull-in.
- Full-screen 3D canvas with overlay HUD instead of permanent sidebar.
- Kept map coordinates (1100×700), converting via scale `S = 28` and `toWorld`/`toMap`.
- Start screen is a two-column character creator with a live 3D preview behind it.
- NPC portraits use animated SVG (blink/breathe/talk) instead of a second WebGL renderer.
- NPC action queue executes in real time with bond/stat updates and reaction barks.
- Combat reuses the Three renderer with a dedicated paper stage, side camera, enemy group, timing strike bar, and shrinking-ring block prompt.
- Parkour uses tweened arcs between defined points; roof zones trigger fall damage when left.
- Save schema replaced with localStorage key `hearthHollow3d`; old `hearthSave` not migrated.
- Shop and inn now have flat walkable rooftops with parapets to support rooftop traversal.

## Work State
### Completed
- New `index.html` UI shell with top bar, HUD, prompt, dynamic action button, joystick, start/customization screen, NPC overlay, generic modal, combat UI, timing minigame, block UI, combat result, toast, fade.
- `styles.css` with desktop/mobile layouts, start screen, NPC overlay/portrait animations, bubbles/queue, combat HUD, minigame/block UI, responsive rules, and `body.combat-mode` HUD hiding.
- `game.js` fully implemented and passes `node --check`:
  - State schema, weapons/outfits/people/buildings/features/mobs/parkour/pickups, utilities, save/load helpers.
  - Renderer/scene/camera/lights, procedural textures, ground/paths/ditch, sky/hills/clouds, well/pond/standing stones, market stalls, farm plot/fences/crops/scarecrow, crates, inn ledge.
  - `createCharacter` with sex/build/skin/hair/beard/outfit/scars, face details, hair styles, backpack for player, walk/idle animation.
  - Player/NPC/mob models, labels, danger rings, building factory with flat/peaked roofs, doors/signs/windows/awnings/parapets, props, pickups, `initWorld`.
  - Input (keyboard, camera drag, pinch/wheel zoom, joystick), camera updates, movement/collision, jump/gravity/fall damage, parkour arcs/roof state.
  - HUD/quests, nearby detection, dynamic action button, feature interactions, building menus, cards, wardrobe, mirror, journal/status.
  - NPC overlay with SVG portraits, mood/barks, action bubbles, live reaction previews, queue playback, bond/romance/marriage/family/work/cards/gift logic.
  - Turn-based combat with side stage, enemy cards, attack/power/mend/flee, timing minigame, active block, victory/defeat, scars, respawn, defeated mob persistence.
  - Start screen customization, plot selection, new/continue flow, time/daylight cycle, daily income, autosave, main animation loop.
- Browser-tested via `playwright-cli` session `hh`; no runtime console errors (only Three.js deprecation warnings and favicon 404).
- Screenshots captured: `screenshots/start.png`, `start2.png`–`start7.png`, `game1.png`–`game4.png`.

### Active
- Tuning start-screen preview and gameplay camera framing/clutter.
- Just changed: removed town-center trees at map `(350,320)` and `(770,350)`; set camera pitch `.3`, distance `7.2`; reduced name-label scale to `1.05 × .27`, enabled depth test, and hid labels within ~7 units.
- These latest edits are not yet reloaded/screenshotted or visually verified.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload page and verify the start-screen preview now shows the player unobstructed; adjust showcase camera target offset/distance if needed.
2. Verify gameplay framing at spawn `(470,340)`, facing east, camera `camYaw = -Math.PI/2`, pitch `.3`, dist `7.2`; ensure NPCs/trees/nameplates do not obscure the player.
3. Test movement, joystick, dynamic action button, NPC conversation queue, and building menus.
4. Test combat end-to-end (attack timing, block, victory/defeat) and parkour (fence/crates/window/ditch, fall damage).
5. Test at 390×844 mobile viewport and fix layout/touch issues.
6. Capture final screenshots only; check for runtime errors after each major interaction.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Main game logic; all systems implemented, currently being visually tuned.
- `index.html`: UI shell; all IDs must stay in sync with `game.js`.
- `styles.css`: Full stylesheet for HUD, start screen, NPC overlay, combat, mobile, combat-mode hiding.
- `vendor/three.min.js`: Local Three.js r152.2.
- `screenshots/`: Latest visual test captures.
- `README.md`: Project description.

- Save key `hearthHollow3d`; defeated mobs stored in `state.defeated`.
- Poly counts are low-poly and within the requested mobile range.
